messages:
sam: noticed a gap in central logs for a handful of egress failures on eu-west1 GPU nodes this morning. Prom alerts fired but kibana search returns no corresponding fluentd entries for some trace_ids. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
lucy: saw the alert too, investigating prometheus -> loki pipeline. which alert and trace_id?
sam: alert=alert:loki_ingest_error_rate:sum increased around 04:12 UTC. sample trace_id=tx-9f3b2aa1. request_id=rid-7c44. Kibana query I tried:
```
kubernetes.pod_name: "gpu-provisioner-*" AND message: /tx-9f3b2aa1/ AND region: "eu-west1"
```
returns zero results. Loki query I ran (approx):
```
{job="fluentd", region="eu-west1"} |= "egress" |~ "tx-9f3b2aa1|rid-7c44"
```
returns nothing as well.
devon: can you paste the prom eval link? might be noise from partial failures. ops-bot: pinging nat-gateway-eu-west1 for current connections and recent restarts.
sre-bot: alert history: alert:loki_ingest_error_rate triggered 2024-09-12T04:11:50Z -> 04:20:03Z, peak rate +12% above threshold.
mike: quick checklist: 1) conntrack saturations on nat? 2) kube-proxy conntrack timeouts? 3) fluentd backpressure or dropped events? 4) kafka partition lag for logs topic?
lucy: checking conntrack on node gpu-rtg-03: `sudo conntrack -S | grep entries` shows entries=980k (limit 1M) — close but not over. syslog shows repeated `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` at 04:10.
sam: ah that's promising — so packets dropped before fluentd saw them. any kube-level NAT changes deployed?
devon: there was a GCE NAT upgrade in the same window (rolling config) per infra-changes.log. might correlate. also saw kube-proxy restart on node gpu-rtg-03 at 04:09 (systemd restart).
lucy: logs from kube-proxy around restart:
```
Sep 12 04:09:03 gpu-rtg-03 kube-proxy[1234]: conntrack flush triggered
Sep 12 04:09:04 gpu-rtg-03 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```
so fluentd never got some egress events.
mike: for next steps: 1) raise conntrack table on affected pool to 2M temporarily, 2) add a short silence for the loki_ingest_error_rate alert for eu-west1 to avoid alert noise while we remediate, 3) rehydrate any missing logs from kafka if retention exists.
sam: I'll bump conntrack sysctl on the node pool and roll out as a DaemonSet sysctl job. prepping PR.
devon: also recommend adding a Kibana saved search for `nf_conntrack` + `gpu-rtg-*` so we can correlate faster.
lucy: tried a manual reingest check: kafka topic `logs-eu-west1` shows producer lag ~0 for that window, so ingress to kafka succeeded. looks like packets dropped before agent.
sam: reingest isn't needed then, but we should update alerting: loki_ingest_error_rate is catching symptoms but not root cause. propose new alert that fires on kernel conntrack drops per-region > 5/min.
mike: agreed — open a quick RFC in #eng-infra for conntrack limits policy. also add runbook steps to the loki alert doc pointing to conntrack checklist.
ops-bot: NAT gateway eu-west1 reports 2 rolling restarts at 04:08 and 04:13 UTC (config push).
lucy: PR for DaemonSet sysctl prepared: `set-nf-conntrack-2m.yaml` — will canary to two nodes first.
sam: thanks — once canary is good, roll. I'll silence the loki alert for 30m while we deploy. :thumbsup:
mike: follow-up: after bump, re-run these queries and paste any sample trace_ids that still return missing logs. we should add a Grafana panel for conntrack usage next to GPU SLO dashboard.
devon: added to my todo for next sprint.
sre-bot: incident-note: created ticket SRE-4321 "eu-west1 conntrack saturation -> missing egress logs".
sam: closing thread for now. ping if something else pops up.
